title: Define Standard Cost Model schema v1 (inputs/outputs), versioning rules, and codegen
creator: Ethan Park
description:
Context
We currently have multiple cost definitions floating around (Console aggregation, billing hooks, Optimize prototypes). This ticket defines the canonical schema for Standard Cost Model v1 so that:
- Console cost breakdowns and Optimize ROI/what-if both call the same API and interpret the same fields.
- Telemetry + runtime exported metrics can be normalized into stable cost primitives.
- Finance can rely on the same breakdown categories for reporting windows.

Scope
Define schema package v1:
1) Request-level inputs (what the cost model needs to compute cost)
2) Request-level outputs (canonical breakdown + totals)
3) Aggregation output shapes (bounded, queryable)
4) What-if input/output shapes (guardrailed)
5) Versioning + compatibility policy (major/minor/patch)
6) Codegen strategy and repo/package layout

Non-goals
- Not implementing the service endpoints (see ENG-4821 / ENG-4824).
- Not replacing billing system of record; these are standardized primitives.

Proposed schema package layout (monorepo)
- package: redwood.costmodel.schema
- versions: v1 (frozen once shipped), v1alpha (if needed for iteration behind flags)
- generated targets: Go (server + client), TypeScript (Console/Optimize), JSON schema for validation + docs

Schema v1: key concepts
A) Determinism and boundedness
- For identical inputs, the model should produce identical outputs (no dependence on wall clock, random sampling, or unbounded lookups).
- Bounded response size: breakdown taxonomy is fixed; any per-dimension breakdown must be top-K with "other" bucket.

B) Versioning and negotiation
- version string is explicit in requests/outputs: schema_version = "cost-model/v1".
- Backward compatibility:
  - Additive fields allowed in minor updates; consumers must ignore unknown fields.
  - Semantics changes require major version bump.
  - Field removals only via deprecation window (>= 2 releases) and major bump.
- Service supports a "min_version"/"max_version" negotiation header in client library (implemented in ENG-4830), but schema package defines the canonical strings and behavior.

C) Canonical identifiers
- model_id: stable Redwood model catalog ID (e.g., "rwqwen2.5-72b-instruct")
- model_revision: immutable revision hash / semver (ties to weights + runtime profile)
- quant_profile_id: stable profile ID from model catalog (ENG-4829)
- deployment_mode: hosted | dedicated | private
- tenant_id, project_id, environment: used for tenancy + routing, not for breakdown grouping by default
- compute_sku: normalized GPU SKU identifier (e.g., "h100-sxm-80gb")

Schema v1: Inputs (RequestCostInput)
Required (v1 must-have)
- request_id: UUID (caller-generated OK)
- timestamp_ms: event time of the request (for joining to telemetry windows; not used for nondeterministic pricing)
- tenant_id, project_id
- deployment_mode
- region
- model_id, model_revision
- quant_profile_id ("fp16" / "int8" / "w4a16" etc. as stable IDs, not free-form)
- token_accounting:
  - prompt_tokens
  - generated_tokens
  - prefill_tokens (if available; otherwise = prompt_tokens)
  - decode_tokens (if available; otherwise = generated_tokens)
  - tokenizer_id (optional; for diagnostics)
- runtime_observations (all optional-but-highly-recommended; if omitted we fall back to default profiles):
  - batch_size_effective_avg
  - queue_time_ms
  - kv_cache_hit_rate (0..1) and kv_cache_bytes_read/write (if available)
  - stage_time_ms_prefill / stage_time_ms_decode (optional; used for sanity checks)
  - fallback_taken: true/false + fallback_reason (if request served by compatible variant)
- routing_context:
  - route_id (Console uses this dimension heavily)
  - policy_id (routing policy version)

Explicitly out of v1 inputs
- No per-layer kernel counters; too high-cardinality and unstable.
- No raw GPU telemetry join keys; those stay in telemetry store, not request payload.

Schema v1: Outputs (RequestCostOutput)
- schema_version
- request_id
- currency: "USD" (v1 fixed; multi-currency later)
- total_cost_usd: decimal string (avoid float; clients must parse)
- breakdown_usd: fixed taxonomy with explicit semantics:
  - compute_prefill_usd
  - compute_decode_usd
  - kv_cache_read_usd
  - kv_cache_write_usd
  - network_egress_usd (0 unless known; v1 can be stubbed)
  - overhead_allocated_usd (allocated platform overhead; see ADR-022 + finance policy)
  - discounts_credits_usd (must be 0 for internal cost; billing can apply separately)
- attribution:
  - cost_basis: "estimated" | "observed" (v1 mostly "estimated"; "observed" allowed for replay/backfill pipelines)
  - confidence: "high" | "medium" | "low" (for Optimize what-if and incomplete runtime observations)
  - warnings: list of warning codes (e.g., "MISSING_KV_CACHE_METRICS", "DEFAULT_BATCH_EFFICIENCY_ASSUMED")

Schema v1: Aggregation (bounded)
- Query shapes live in the API design spec, but schema must include canonical response types:
  - AggregatedCostBreakdown: totals + breakdown by fixed dimensions (route_id, model_id, deployment_mode) with top-K semantics.
  - Always include "other" bucket when top-K is used.
  - Include sample_count and token totals to support dashboard normalization.

Schema v1: What-if inputs/outputs
- WhatIfCostInput:
  - baseline_workload_summary: {prompt_tokens_p50/p95, decode_tokens_p50/p95, qps_avg, concurrency_avg} (encoded as flat fields in schema; avoid nested maps)
  - baseline_config: {batching_enabled, caching_enabled, quant_profile_id}
  - proposed_config: same fields
  - constraints: {max_p95_latency_ms, min_quality_tier}
- WhatIfCostOutput:
  - baseline_total_cost_usd
  - proposed_total_cost_usd
  - delta_usd
  - delta_percent
  - confidence and assumptions: list of assumption codes (e.g., "CACHE_WARM_RATE_ASSUMED_0P7")

Notes on overhead allocation (v1)
- Overhead is explicitly shown as overhead_allocated_usd.
- v1 policy: allocate overhead proportionally to request-attributable compute (prefill+decode) within a reporting window; exact policy parameters are not embedded in schema, but output must carry an overhead_policy_id string for auditability.

Codegen + validation
- Generate:
  - Go types + JSON marshal/unmarshal with strict validation (unknown fields allowed, but required fields enforced)
  - TypeScript types for Console/Optimize
  - JSON Schema artifact for docs and conformance tests
- Validation rules (examples):
  - token counts >= 0
  - confidence enum constrained
  - kv_cache_hit_rate in [0,1]
  - cost fields are decimal strings with max 6 fractional digits

Reviewers / sign-off
- Console: Chloe Martin, Jada Williams (confirm required fields for breakdown pages; ensure response shapes support top-K and "other")
- Optimize: Aditya Rao, Jonas Weber (confirm what-if fields and confidence/assumptions model)
- Telemetry: Logan Wright, Nadia Rahman (confirm availability of runtime_observations and token splits)
- Finance: Laura Bennett/Rishi Malhotra (confirm overhead representation and auditability)

Acceptance criteria
- Schema v1 types merged as a versioned package with docs comments describing semantics (especially overhead_allocated_usd, prefill vs decode, cache read/write).
- Codegen outputs present for Go + TS, and serialization tests pass.
- Conformance tests include at least 5 golden examples covering: cache hit, cache miss, batching effect, quant profile change, fallback route.
- Review approvals recorded from Console + Optimize.

Links
- PRD: sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/standard-cost-model-prd.json
- API design spec: sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/cost-model-api-v1-design-spec.json
- ADR-021: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-021-standardize-cost-model-interfaces.json
- ADR-022: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-022-cost-breakdown-taxonomy.json
- Proto outline (early): sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/platform-engineering/cost-model-api-proto-outline.json

Implementation notes / decisions made in this ticket
- Use decimal strings for money fields to avoid float drift across languages.
- Keep taxonomy fields explicit (no map<string, number>) to ensure boundedness and stable dashboards.
- Prefer stable IDs (quant_profile_id, compute_sku) rather than free-form strings for long-lived analytics.

Follow-ups
- If runtime cannot provide prefill/decode split reliably, v1 must define fallback semantics (prefill=prompt_tokens, decode=generated_tokens) and surface warning code.
- If network egress cannot be measured per request, keep network_egress_usd at 0 in v1 and document it as "not modeled".
comments: 2026-01-10 (Ethan Park): Kicking off schema work. Please keep fields explicit; we got bitten before by map-based breakdowns blowing up cardinality and dashboards.

2026-01-13 (Chloe Martin): Console needs (1) route_id always present, (2) top-K breakdown by model_id within a time range, (3) explicit prefill vs decode numbers. Please include sample_count and token totals in aggregated response types so we can normalize per 1k tokens.

2026-01-15 (Aditya Rao): For Optimize what-if, we need a place to express confidence + assumptions. Not every projection is equally reliable; please include a structured list of assumption codes, even if it’s just strings in v1.

2026-01-18 (Nadia Rahman): Token split availability: prompt_tokens and generated_tokens are reliable; prefill/decode split depends on runtime export (ENG-4828/PR-28509). Suggest schema marks prefill/decode optional but defines fallback semantics + warning code.

2026-01-22 (Laura Bennett): Finance requirement: overhead must be explicit and auditable. Add overhead_policy_id and make sure discounts/credits are not mixed into internal cost; billing can overlay later.

2026-02-03 (Benji Okafor): Drafted schema comments + validation rules. Using decimal strings for costs, enums for confidence/cost_basis, and stable IDs for model/quant. Will send for final review once codegen is wired.

2026-02-12 (Jada Williams): Please document that overhead_allocated_usd may not sum perfectly at the single-request level due to windowed allocation, but aggregates should reconcile within tolerance. Add note to docs comments.
2026-02-18 (Ethan Park): Marking done after merge of schema package + serialization tests. Next: service wiring + client library version negotiation.
